newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle seen steady to off, feeders mixed.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle seen steady to off, feeders mixed.

text.p: CME live cattle futures were expected to open steady to 0.150 cent per lb lower while feeder cattle calls ranged mixed, from 0.100 higher to 0.100 lower, livestock analysts said.

Carryover pressure is expected in live cattle futures following active feedlot sales at lower prices Tuesday. Feedlots sold slaughter-ready cattle at $63 per cwt, down $1 from the bulk of sales last week and the trend looks lower going into July, sources said.
Boxed beef values also are trending lower which will keep packer bids lower, they said.
Futures were also approaching major chart points which could ignite sell stops, sources noted.
Some analysts look for early strength in feeder cattle futures following the upturn in the latest CME feeder cattle index to a new high for the recent move and on indications of lower corn futures.
Feedlots remain willing to pay up for feeders despite the easier tone to fed cattle, they said.
However, others look for action in live cattle futures to influence trade which could bring mixed prices.
The latest CME feeder cattle index rose $0.59 per cwt to $77.56, the highest since August 18, 1994.
